plain_text:
HEALTH TIPS Though most children and teenagers
have had less severe cases of COVID-19 compared with
adults, they can still get sick and spread the disease to
other people.
semantic_text: HEALTH TIPS Though most children and teenagers have had less severe cases of COVID-19 compared with adults, they can still get sick and spread the disease to other people.

plain_text:
That's why COVID-19 vaccines are important for children
and teens who are eligible. Currently, the Centers for
Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends that
everyone age 12 and older be vaccinated against COVID-19.
Widespread vaccination is our best hope to prevent
COVID-19 from spreading.
semantic_text: That's why COVID-19 vaccines are important for children and teens who are eligible. Currently, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends that everyone age 12 and older be vaccinated against COVID-19. Widespread vaccination is our best hope to prevent COVID-19 from spreading.

plain_text:
Vaccines help us develop immunity to the virus that causes
COVID-19 without needing to get the illness. By getting
vaccinated, people of all ages make it harder for the virus
to spread from person to person. Much of the science and
research behind some of the COVID-19 vaccines started with
research that began before the pandemic on other viruses,
like those that cause the cold and flu.

plain_text:
The COVID-19 vaccine has mild, temporary side effects
and does not cause COVID-19.
semantic_text: The COVID-19 vaccine has mild, temporary side effects and does not cause COVID-19.

plain_text:
Everyone in the U.S., including children who are eligible,
can get a free COVID-19 vaccination, regardless of
immigration or health insurance status.
semantic_text: Everyone in the U.S., including children who are eligible, can get a free COVID-19 vaccination, regardless of immigration or health insurance status.

plain_text:
Currently, all children 12 and older are permitted to
get the Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine, which is a two-part
vaccine series. People need both doses of this vaccine
before they are considered fully vaccinated; they are also
not considered fully vaccinated until 14 days after their
second dose. Before your child gets their vaccination,

Before your child gets their vaccination,

plain_text:
check with your local pharmacy to see if appointments
are available or if you can just walk in. Your health care
provider may also offer COVID-19 vaccines.

plain_text:
Talk to your child about what to expect from the vaccination.
Side effects such as a sore arm, injection site swelling,
tiredness, and headache may affect your child's ability to do
some daily activities. The effects should go away in a few
days. Many people have no side effects or reactions.
semantic_text: Talk to your child about what to expect from the vaccination. Many people have no side effects or reactions.

plain_text:
The CDC does not recommend taking ibuprofen, aspirin,
or acetaminophen before vaccination for the purpose of
trying to prevent vaccine-related side effects. It's also good
to speak with your child's health care provider if you have
any questions or to confirm any potential allergies.
